# Matching models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

12 matching models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 768x1024: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## FlexGlue

FlexGlue (ETH Zurich and partners, 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: ALIKED keypoints, DINOv3 ConvNeXt features and a transformer that predicts where each keypoint lands in the other photo; keypoint index pairs. MIT; DINOv3 backbone weights under the DINOv3 licence.

Commercial use: yes.

Speed and memory not measured for: `aliked-flexglue`.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/cvg/FlexGlue> at `99920296d082`
- Code licence: MIT AND BSD-3-Clause (permissive); files: `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-ALIKED`, `LICENSE-DINOv3`
- Weights licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License AND BSD-3-Clause
- Licence evidence: https://github.com/cvg/FlexGlue/blob/99920296d082c9405ebfd612d674efe288e74881/README.md#license ; https://github.com/Shiaoming/ALIKED/blob/683d7c65197395c0b3f01ebe76e1084a27e73a65/LICENSE
- Training data: FlexGlue: the README states no training data and the training code is not released (see the paper). The DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone was pretrained on LVD-1689M (Meta, not released); ALIKED was trained on MegaDepth.
- Licence note: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone weights (`extractor.backbone.*`): the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers them; read it before commercial use.
- Options: `max_keypoints` = 2048 (>= 1), `long_side` = 1024 (>= 0), `size` = 512 (>= 32)
- Kernel libraries: none (not implemented: data-dependent keypoint and match counts)
- Variants: `aliked-flexglue`
- Outputs: keypoints1, keypoints2, pairs, scores
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `aliked-flexglue` 3000x4000 (2.0 GiB peak allocated, 2.5 reserved)

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0052 and p99 <= 0.012 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aliked-flexglue` | no kernels backend | - | - |

### Limitations

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
- No exportable module: the keypoint and match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
- Upstream's sparse mode only: no RoMa v2 refiner, no dense or sampled matches and no covisibility score.
- Two resizes per image as upstream: ALIKED sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.

</details>

## DeDoDe v2

Commercial use: yes.

## LoFTR

LoFTR (Zhejiang University, CVPR 2021): detector-free matching of two photos of one scene with transformers; semi-dense matches as keypoint pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Outdoor (MegaDepth) and indoor (ScanNet) weights. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

### Limitations

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; every match is its own keypoint pair (`pairs` is `[[0, 0], [1, 1], ...]`).
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
- No exportable module: the match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
- Images are converted to grayscale and matched at `long_side` (default 840, upstream's MegaDepth test size); the coarse matching holds an (H W / 64)^2 score matrix, so memory grows with the 4th power of the side. The indoor weights were evaluated by upstream at 640 x 480 (ScanNet).

</details>

## RoMa

RoMa (2024): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv2 and a VGG19. MIT code and weights; the DINOv2 weights are Apache-2.0.

Commercial use: yes.

<a id="romav2"></a>

## RoMa v2

RoMa v2 (2025): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv3. MIT code; the DINOv3 parts of the code and weights are under the DINOv3 licence.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `romav2` | synthetic (768x1024) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 1412<br>741<br>546<br>406<br>576<br>353 | 11159 / 11606<br>9881 / 10124<br>1989 / 2596<br>1909 / 2580<br>3150 / 3386<br>6694 / 6740 |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/Parskatt/romav2> at `95c9968145c8`
- Code licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License (permissive); files: `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`
- Weights licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License
- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/Parskatt/romav2/blob/95c9968145c8906b7b59383258e9f73b02853d89/README.md#license>
- Training data: Upstream README: a mix of wide-baseline matching datasets following UFM and MapAnything (MegaDepth and others; see the paper); none has a dataset entry here yet. The frozen DINOv3 descriptor was pretrained on LVD-1689M (not released).
- Licence note: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ViT-L/16 weights, and net/dinov3.py and net/vit/ come from DINOv3: the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers those parts; read it before commercial use.
- Options: `coarse_size` = 800 (>= 16), `fine_size` = 1280 (>= 0), `keep_descriptors` = 0 (>= 0; speed only)
- Kernel libraries: `romav2`
- Variants: `romav2`
- Outputs: warp, certainty
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `romav2` 3000x4000 (2.9 GiB peak allocated, 4.7 reserved)
- `romav2` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 254 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 185 s (ONNX + engine).
- `romav2` original (fp32) 768x1024: upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)
- `romav2` original 768x1024: the authors' mixed-precision option (bfloat16); upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)
- `romav2` load / first call: original 5.45 s / 2.091 s, portable 0.85 s / 0.913 s, kernels 1.5 s / 0.812 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

## XFeat

XFeat (Verlab, CVPR 2024): fast sparse keypoints and descriptors, matched by mutual nearest neighbours or LighterGlue; output as keypoints plus index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xfeat` | synthetic (768x1024) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 8.89<br>8.35<br>–<br>5.65<br>fails: ONNX export: conversion failed | 128 / 174<br>186 / 214<br>–<br>186 / 212<br>– |
| `xfeat-lighterglue` | synthetic (768x1024) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 23.6<br>22.5<br>–<br>16.2<br>fails: ONNX export: torch.export failed | 448 / 478<br>444 / 476<br>–<br>262 / 278<br>– |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/verlab/accelerated_features> at `e92685f57f83`
- Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: Apache-2.0
- Licence evidence: https://github.com/verlab/accelerated_features/blob/e92685f57f8318b18725c5c8c0bd28c7fe188d9a/LICENSE ; https://github.com/verlab/accelerated_features/blob/e92685f57f8318b18725c5c8c0bd28c7fe188d9a/README.md#license
- Training data: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth), COCO 2017 (train, instance annotations) (XFeat: MegaDepth and synthetic warps of a 20k-image COCO 2017 subset (README training section). LighterGlue: trained with GlueFactory (README; MegaDepth, data not otherwise stated).)
- Options: `max_keypoints` = 4096 (>= 1), `long_side` = 0 (>= 0)
- Kernel libraries: none (not implemented: data-dependent keypoint counts (NMS, top-k, match filtering); the extractor is a small CNN)
- Variants: `xfeat`, `xfeat-lighterglue`
- Outputs: keypoints1, keypoints2, pairs, scores
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `xfeat` 3000x4000 (1.0 GiB peak allocated, 1.2 reserved); `xfeat-lighterglue` 3000x4000 (1.0 GiB peak allocated, 1.2 reserved)
- `xfeat` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 31 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `xfeat-lighterglue` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 40 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `xfeat` original 768x1024: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream XFeat.detectAndCompute + mnn, top_k 4096
- `xfeat-lighterglue` original 768x1024: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; upstream XFeat.detectAndCompute + lighterglue, top_k 4096
- `xfeat` load / first call: original 1.51 s / 0.629 s, portable 0.04 s / 0.565 s
- `xfeat-lighterglue` load / first call: original 1.46 s / 0.692 s, portable 0.07 s / 0.635 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `xfeat` | MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees | 29.1 / 46.1 / 60.8 | 28.4 / 44.6 / 60.1 | 29.1 / 46.1 / 60.8 |  |
| `xfeat-lighterglue` | MegaDepth-1500, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees |  |  | 39.7 / 57.5 / 72.8 |  |
| `xfeat-lighterglue` | MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees | 42.0 / 59.4 / 74.3 | 42.7 / 60.1 / 74.1 | 42.0 / 59.4 / 74.3 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks ec7b1307+port/p1-match, 2026-11-12.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 3e-05 vs the original. GPU, portable float32 and kernels float16 (the defaults): mean |diff| <= 0.0001 and p99 <= 0.001 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xfeat` | no kernels backend | - | - |
| `xfeat-lighterglue` | no kernels backend | - | - |

### Limitations

- Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
- One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
- No exportable module: the keypoint counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
- `xfeat` (mutual nearest neighbours) has no learned confidence: its scores are the descriptors' cosine similarities.

</details>
